definition: A professional sumo tournament, held six times each year.
The ring where sumo bouts are held.
The heavy silk belt wrestlers wear during bouts.
A wrestler's ring name.
A winning record in a basho, usually 8+ wins.
A losing record in a basho, usually 8+ losses.
A tournament championship.
A wrestler's win-loss score chart during a tournament.
A sidestep at the tachiai to evade the opponent's charge.
The initial charge at the start of a bout.
A professional sumo wrestler, literally meaning 'powerful man.'
A sumo stable where wrestlers live, train, and are managed under a single stablemaster.
The referee who officiates sumo bouts, carrying a war fan to signal decisions.
The official ranking document listing all wrestlers in order of rank, hand-written before each tournament.
The top division in professional sumo, containing a maximum of 42 wrestlers.
A wrestler ranked in the top two divisions who receives a full salary and special privileges.
A sumo stablemaster, typically a retired senior wrestler, who trains and manages all wrestlers in his stable.
One of the six official grand tournaments held each year in Japan, each lasting 15 days.
Sumo training practice, conducted daily inside the stable's practice ring.
The formal ring-entering ceremony performed by wrestlers before each day's bouts begin.
A heavily embroidered ceremonial apron worn by sekitori during the dohyo-iri ring-entering ceremony.
A 'gold star' award and permanent salary bonus earned by a maegashira who defeats a yokozuna.
The five ringside judges who monitor bouts and may convene a mono-ii if the outcome is disputed.
A formal deliberation called by the ringside judges to review a close or disputed match decision.
The wooden war fan carried by the gyoji, used to signal the start of a bout and point to the winner.
The rice-straw bales embedded in the clay that mark the circular boundary of the dohyo.
The officially declared winning technique used to end a sumo bout, chosen from 82 recognized moves.
The probationary status of an ozeki who must win 8+ bouts in the next tournament to avoid demotion.
An official absence from a tournament, typically due to injury, which can affect a wrestler's ranking.
A perfect tournament championship won without a single defeat across all 15 bouts.
Three special prizes awarded each tournament for fighting spirit, technique, and outstanding performance.
The 'Fighting Spirit Prize,' awarded to a wrestler showing exceptional tenacity in a tournament.
The 'Technique Prize,' awarded to a wrestler demonstrating superior technical skill in a tournament.
The 'Outstanding Performance Prize,' awarded to a lower-ranked wrestler who defeats multiple top-ranked opponents.
Sponsor banners paraded around the ring before a high-profile bout, representing prize money for the winner.
The traditional hot-pot stew eaten by sumo wrestlers in large quantities to build body mass.
The traditional topknot hairstyle worn by sumo wrestlers, required by the Japan Sumo Association.
The retirement ceremony in which a wrestler's topknot is ceremonially cut by invited guests and the stablemaster.
An exhibition tour held between official tournaments where wrestlers perform in regional venues across Japan.
A rapid, alternating open-palm thrusting attack used to batter an opponent backward.
A grappling style in which both wrestlers grip each other's mawashi and fight at close range.
A thrusting and pushing style of sumo that avoids belt grips, relying on palm strikes and body pressure.
A false start, called when one wrestler charges before both hands are simultaneously on the starting lines.
The final and most dramatic day of a tournament, when the yusho champion is decided.
The final and most prestigious bout of each tournament day, featuring the highest-ranked wrestlers.
An individual sumo bout scheduled on the day's official program.
An open-fisted slap to an opponent's face, used as a distraction or to knock them off balance.
A rematch ordered by the judges when a bout's outcome is too close or unclear to determine a winner.
The flat cushion spectators sit on; traditionally thrown into the ring by fans after an upset victory over a yokozuna.
A leg-strengthening training exercise where wrestlers raise each leg high and stamp it powerfully into the ground.
The main sumo arena in Tokyo's Ryogoku district, hosting three of the six annual grand tournaments.
